• **wjnc的观点**：对文章的信息量不足表示失望，提出了一系列关于反应规模、能量释放、时间跨度及可见性等问题。并通过Claude和Wikipedia获取补充信息，确认了反应堆平均热功率为100千瓦。

• **foobarian的观点**：讨论了奥克洛铀矿中铀-235的含量微小差异，引发了对测量误差范围的兴趣，并幽默地表示如果是垃圾软件开发者可能会忽视这种微小差异。

• **Aardwolf的观点**：进一步探讨了天然铀中铀-235含量的普遍性，提出了是否与太阳系形成时的超新星爆炸有关，并进一步思考银河系其他部分或外来物质对地球的影响。

补充讨论：
• **kkwteh的观点**：半开玩笑地提出奥克洛的天然核反应堆可能是古代文明或核战争的遗迹。

• **stmw的观点**：提到了一家名为Oklo的创业公司，该公司制造被动安全的核反应堆，将历史与现代科技联系起来。

• **HelloUsername的观点**：提供了一个2018年的相关链接，引导读者查看更多讨论。

• **eabeezxjc的观点**：附和kkwteh的观点，认为可能是动荡时期核战争的遗迹。

• **fnord77的观点**：提出一个有趣的问题，即奥克洛是已知的唯一天然核反应堆，而恒星是否也可以被视为天然核反应堆。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在奥克洛现象的科学意义及其对现代核废料处理的启示。一些人认为这是核废料可以安全埋藏的证据，而另一些人则关注信息不足，希望了解更多具体数据和背景信息。

• 对天然铀中铀-235含量微小差异的测量误差及其可能的宇宙学意义存在讨论。

• 半开玩笑的古代文明或核战争遗迹的猜测引发了轻松的讨论，但并未被严肃对待。

data.title: Apple typewriter memo (2020)
data.author: rafaepta
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了苹果公司早期CEO Mike Scott的职业生涯及其影响，包括他试图终止Macintosh项目和在“黑色星期三”解雇40名员工的举动，之后他自己也被解雇。Scott后来成为宝石专家，一种矿物以他的名字命名。文章提到Scott的一份备忘录，通过纸质形式分发，可能使用Apple II打印，并指出备忘录中有拼写错误。文中还讨论了备忘录中提到的"Ken"可能是谁，以及当时使用的文字处理设备，如Digital Equipment Corporation的字处理器和Apple II的Apple Writer系统。文章最后提到，尽管技术进步，打字机仍未完全被淘汰，某些老式打字机仍在使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对技术设备（如打字机、文字处理器等）的使用体验和历史演变的不同看法

不同观点：
• yosef123：认为公司禁止打字机的举动并不负面，反而表明公司对其产品有信心，并可能希望改进产品。他指出，当产品不被其创造者使用时，用户体验往往不好。

• squelchy5000：批评文字处理器的设计不够人性化，特别是长文档处理时，用户需要从上到下滚动，而不是让文本自动上滚，这与打字机相比失去了某些优点。

• PaulHoule：分享了个人经历，讲述了早期的计算机设备如PDP-8/A和VT-61终端的使用体验，以及这些设备在特定场景（如小报社的排版）中的应用。他认为尽管Apple ][+在某些方面优于PDP-8/A，但PDP-8/A的终端具有80列显示的优势。

• mproud：认为讨论中的文章具有讽刺意味，目的更多是为了幽默，而不是严肃的讨论。他指出，文章表面上是在推崇打字机，实际上却是在Apple产品上写的，带有调侃性质。

• ginko：对打字机是否过时提出质疑，认为打字机在自己的专业领域中已经很少见，并表示对打字机的使用感到陌生。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对打字机和现代文字处理器的实用性有不同看法。squelchy5000和ginko认为打字机已经过时或不如现代设备好用，而yosef123和PaulHoule则在某种程度上认可打字机或早期计算设备的历史价值和特定场景下的优势。

• 争议焦点在于打字机是否真的过时以及现代文字处理器的设计是否充分考虑了用户体验。squelchy5000对现代处理器的设计提出了具体批评，而ginko则质疑打字机在当代的实际应用价值。

• mproud强调了文章的幽默性质，提醒读者不要过于认真对待讨论内容，这也为整个讨论增加了一层轻松的氛围。

44340790.article_content:
.
.. and typewriters
still
aren't obsolete!
A few memos about the memo:
•
Mike Scott
served as the first CEO of Apple, from February 1977 to March 1981. His other fine judgments include trying to shut down the Macintosh project and firing 40 employees on so-called "Black Wednesday," a move that he claimed would make the company "fun" again. He himself was fired as CEO shortly thereafter. However, "Scotty" has enjoyed a brilliant later career as an
expert on gemstones
. The mineral
Scottyite
, a barium copper silicate, was named in his honor.
• Scotty's memo evidently was distributed on paper, using a pre-printed form. I assume it was typed on an Apple II, but I am not sure. Apparently his writing device didn't have spell-check (note the misspelling "priorty" and the three spaces between "and" and "convince").
• It's possible that "Ken" was
Ken Rothmuller
, who was the Lisa project manager at the time. But Mr. Rothmuller tells me that he doesn't recall the memo or using a DEC word processor, and that most of the Lisa team would have been using the Apple II for writing.  He is not aware of another Ken working at Apple in 1980, but it's possible that there was a Ken in the main building; the Lisa team worked in a different building. Mr. Rothmuller adds that although Scott was the CEO, Steve Jobs was actually making a lot of the decisions.
• Ken's Digital Equipment Corporation word processor probably looked something like this (
source
). (In the early '60s, DEC had developed one of the first word-processing programs, humorously called
Expensive Typewriter
.)
• "Apple II-Apple Writer Systems":
Apple Writer
(1979) was a word-processing application for the Apple II computer. It displayed text only in uppercase, though capitalized letters could be highlighted. What a beautiful advancement over typewriters, eh?
• "Apple high performance systems" just seems to be a general category that makes a vague promise about future advancements.
• Scott's phrase "direct typing capabilities" doesn't seem to exist anywhere outside this memo, but I think he meant the ability to type immediately onto paper, with no word processing intervening between the keyboard and the printing.
•
Qume
was a leading manufacturer of daisy-wheel printers. Did "Qume with Keyboard/Apple installations" mean a setup that allowed the Qume printer to function like a typewriter (immediately printing when you hit a key)? Qume did produce some computer monitors and keyboards at some point in the '80s, but I imagine Apple wouldn't be using those.
Four decades later, what has happened? Apple, of course, successfully developed the Mac, and found new prosperity and influence in the 21st century thanks to the iPod, iPad, and iPhone. There is an
Apple II aficionado group on Facebook
with over 7000 members. Typewriters have been relegated to the margins of business, but many businesses still keep one around. Electronic and manual typewriters are still manufactured. And the great, durable mid-20th-century typewriters are still clacking away....

data.title: Maple Mono: open-source monospace font with round corner
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: Maple Mono是一款开源的圆角等宽字体，专为编程设计，支持连字和控制台图标，具有细粒度的自定义选项。该字体提供可变的字重和斜体字形，中英文宽度比例为2:1，适合多语言显示和Markdown表格。它支持Nerd-Font，使终端更生动，并针对IDE和终端进行了优化。用户可以通过多种包管理器如Scoop、Homebrew和ArchLinuxCN安装不同版本的Maple Mono，包括中文版（CN）和常规版。该字体在GitHub上获得了17.3k星标和561次 fork，具有广泛的社区支持。

Maple Mono
Maple Mono is an open source monospace font focused on smoothing your coding flow.
I create it to enhance my working experience, and hope that it can be useful to others.
V7 is a completely remade version, providing variable font format and source files of font project, redesigning more than half of the glyphs and offering smarter ligatures. You can checkout V6
here
Features
✨ Variable - Infinity font weights with fine-grained italic glyphs.
☁️ Smooth - Round corner, brand-new glyph of
@ $ % & Q ->
and cursive
f i j k l x y
in italic style.
💪 Useful - Large amount of smart ligatures, see in
features/
🎨 Icon - First-Class
Nerd-Font
support, make your terminal more vivid.
🔨 Customize - Enable or disable font features as you want, just make your own font.
Simpified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and Japanese
CN version based on
Resource Han Rounded
provides complete character set support for Chinese development environments, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and Japanese. Meanwhile, the characteristic of perfect 2:1 alignment between Chinese and English allows this font to achieve a neat, uniform, beautiful, and comfortable appearance in scenarios such as multilingual display and Markdown tables. However, the spacing of Chinese characters is larger compared to other popular Chinese fonts. See details in
release notes
and

.

data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕机器人技术及其历史、应用、技术挑战等展开的讨论

不同观点：
• [Symmetry] 认为文章遗漏了一个重要事件，即Boston Dynamics的机器人被枪击的事件，并提供了相关新闻链接。此外，他还补充了一个关于编程语言启发的链接，为文章提供了背景信息。
• [z3ratul163071] 对文章中提到的ROS操作系统发表评论，认为文章隐藏了一个有趣的点，即ROS虽然被广泛使用，但一些公司和研究人员难以从该系统迁移出去。
• [modeless] 讨论了Google在机器人领域的收购及其后续发展，认为Google在解雇Andy Rubin后失去了对机器人项目的耐心，导致项目停滞并最终被出售给SoftBank。他认为高层管理支持的缺乏是失败的原因。
• [nsxwolf] 对文章标题表示质疑，不确定这篇文章是否是某种形式的“如何避免”指南，显示出对文章实际内容的困惑。
• [ianbicking] 提出了关于远程临场技术为何没有普及的问题，引发对技术应用场景的讨论。
• [degrees57] 分享了个人经历，提到Odetics的Odex 1机器人，并描述了其参与的一个展示活动，补充了文章未涉及的历史细节。
• [mooseling] 表达了在情感低谷时对类似文章的喜爱，并请求更多类似内容推荐，显示出对轻松且易于理解的技术文章的需求。
• [smath] 提出了一个技术性问题，询问让机器人叠衣服或洗碗的最佳方法，显示出对具体机器人应用的关注。
• [outside1234] 以幽默的方式评论了Tesla的Optimus机器人部署情况，暗示其高成本和低效率的问题，批评了其实际应用价值。
• [taneq] 对文章中的幽默和回溯性定义（如AI的滑稽反义解释）表示欣赏，提出了对AI定义变化的思考。
• [gdiamos] 质疑文章是否由ChatGPT生成，反映了当前对AI生成内容的关注和讨论。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是Google在机器人项目上的管理和决策，特别是解雇Andy Rubin对项目的影响。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对ROS操作系统在研究和商业应用中的实际挑战，以及其广泛使用和难以迁移的问题。
• 评论中还涉及了对具体机器人应用（如远程临场、家务机器人）的兴趣和疑问，显示出对技术实际应用的关注。
• 幽默和个人故事在评论中也扮演了重要角色，反映出读者对轻松且具有人情味的内容的偏好。

data.article_summary: 《在西弗吉尼亚，灰狗赛跑的复杂历史与不确定未来》一文探讨了美国最后一个活跃的灰狗赛道所在的州，传统与不确定性并存。文章描述了赛狗的古老渊源，它们曾被多个古代文明所喜爱，因其高贵和狩猎能力而备受珍视。然而，如今的赛狗行业在西弗吉尼亚州面临衰退。文章提到，尽管观看赛狗的人数大幅减少，根据州规定，赛道每年仍需举办至少200天比赛。自佛罗里达州在2019年禁止赛狗以来，西弗吉尼亚的赛狗业更加萧条。文章质疑，既然赛狗不再为公司带来可观收入，为何它们仍在奔跑？这涉及赌博合法化的历史和社会许可的变化。灰狗赛跑曾是非法活动，但在大萧条时期被合法化，尽管面临道德和动物福利方面的反对。如今，这一行业面临存续问题，反映了其社会和经济合法性的逐渐丧失。

Two greyhounds at night
, 2019, oil on panel by Clare Menck © The artist. Courtesy 99 Loop Gallery
Issue 129, Summer 2025
May 23, 2025
The Tangled Past and Unsettled Future of Greyhound Racing in West Virginia
In the home of America’s last active tracks, tradition and uncertainty run neck and neck
By Michelle Orange
This story appears in the Summer 2025 print edition with the title “Comely in Going.
” O
rder the Y’all Street Issue
here
.
T
hey look ancient because they are.
Eight in all, each one led by a teenaged handler in a royal purple t-shirt, the dogs cut a silhouette at odds with their surroundings. Moving from the paddock to the gated starting blocks, they squat and sniff and occasionally bark, appearing most themselves, or most familiar, when flattened in profile: the elegant, tapered snout, stretched-out torso, and tiny waist; the massive haunches and sickle-shaped curve of the belly. The same stark, primeval outlines can be found in Roman mosaics and temple drawings dating back to 6000 BC. The Greeks, the Celts, the Egyptians—they all loved the greyhound, or its close relations. Bred and cherished for its perceived nobility as much as its hunting prowess, no dog has been depicted as frequently, across as many millennia, or by a broader range of humans.
Signs of that linkage are scarce on an August afternoon in Wheeling, West Virginia, home to one of this country’s two remaining active greyhound racetracks. Yet despite the shambling, urine-soaked starting-block procession and barren, unsplendid backdrop, there persists a sense of something wondrous happening, of watching eight walking hieroglyphs pass by.
Earlier, inside the viewing bay—an eerily quiet, glass-enclosed grandstand where roughly two dozen people sat hunched, in clusters and alone, marking their betting sheets and sampling concessions—I stood with Kim Florence, the president and general manager of Wheeling Island Hotel, Casino & Racetrack, and Glen White, a representative of Delaware North, the resort’s Buffalo-based parent company. There, we passed the last ten minutes of our hour together pointedly not talking about the thing we were there to talk about. Behind us, a handful of old men sat facing a wall of television screens simulcasting horse races from around the country. Below us, a tomato-red dirt Zamboni groomed the 548-yard track during the eleven-minute break before the next of the afternoon’s eighteen greyhound races, each of which lasts about thirty seconds.
If these dogs are no longer driving company revenue, why are they still running?
Time was, even ten or fifteen years ago, Wheeling Island ran thirty races a day. By state mandate, they must hold live races on no fewer than two hundred days each year. Since 2019, the year after Florida voters approved an amendment to ban greyhound racing at the eleven remaining tracks in that state, the already diminished number of racing patrons at Wheeling Island has declined by more than half. These numbers are not the stuff of happy executives, or budget meetings. Florence and White had agreed to meet with me but asked that the details of our conversation be off the record. Our tour of the facility included a stop inside the track kennel, where 144 dogs made a proportional racket from within their stacked wire enclosures, and the adjoining adoption kennel, where eighteen former racers snoozed in individual stalls behind a purple velvet curtain. Meant to showcase the track’s orderly and humane operation, the tour had also circled, in purely corporate terms, the question at hand: If these dogs are no longer driving company revenue, why are they still running?
T
he answer requires an unfolding of the origami compact by which certain pursuits gain and lose legitimacy—acquiring social and legal licenses and then, less often, especially if they are profitable, having one or both licenses taken away. The history of wagering in the U.S. is one such compact: Once the purview of gangsters and their prey, gambling in some form is now legal, and indeed a source of government revenue, in all but two states. The history of greyhound racing is another: By 1930, ten years after a man named Owen Patrick Smith opened the first commercially recognized greyhound track in the country, in Emeryville, California, there were sixty-seven such tracks in operation—all of them illegal. Five years after that, Depression-era economics had changed the political calculus: Florida, Oregon, and Massachusetts had all legalized dog racing; twenty more states were to follow, despite moral and personal objections voiced by various legislators, church groups, and animal welfare organizations along the way. Though dog racing lacked the glamour and prestige of horse racing and never became as popular, greyhounds were easier to breed and less expensive to keep. data.title: Minimal auto-differentiation engine in Rust
data.author: lschneider
data.article_summary: **nanograd** 是一个用Rust编写的最小自动微分引擎。它通过定义 `Scalar` 结构体来实现，每个 `Scalar` 存储值、可选的梯度以及生成它的操作描述。通过操作符重载（如 `+`、`*`、`-` 等）和 `scalar::func` 中的辅助函数，构建出一个由 `Scalar` 节点组成的有向无环图（DAG）。调用 `backward()` 方法可以从输出节点开始递归地传播梯度，并累积到通过 `Scalar::new_grad` 创建的叶子节点中。该项目包含一个训练小型多层感知机（MLP）学习XOR功能的演示，并能通过 `plot::dump_graph` 将计算图可视化为一个包含D3.js的HTML文件。项目使用MIT许可证，目前获得44个星标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于自动微分中全局/共享状态的改变及其潜在问题，以及对项目设计和实现的讨论

不同观点：
• **amelius的观点**：提出关于全局/共享状态的改变可能会导致问题。具体来说，当多个函数同时进行反向传播（backward pass），并且这些函数依赖于相同的变量（如x和y）时，收集这些变量的偏导数（partial derivatives）可能会出现冲突。amelius认为更好的设计是使用z.get_grad(x)和w.get_grad(x)这种方式，分别获取每个函数对变量的偏导数，而不是直接通过x.get_grad()这种共享方式。

• **tnlogy的观点**：对项目表示赞赏，并分享了自己曾经做过的一个类似的小项目，目的是学习Rust和复习机器学习知识。虽然最初计划将计算图存储在堆中以便后续发送到GPU上执行，但因为某些原因（如懒惰）而放弃了该计划。tnlogy强调，即使项目未完成，也能从中学习到东西。

• **kragen的观点**：认为在标题中加入"backward-mode"（反向模式）会更有助于理解。这个观点主要是针对文档或项目命名提出的小建议，旨在让读者更容易明白项目涉及的核心概念。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于共享状态在多线程环境下的安全性，amelius认为直接使用共享变量收集偏导数可能导致错误结果，而未直接提出解决方案，只是建议通过更明确的方式获取每个函数的偏导数。
• tnlogy的评论更多是个人经验分享，没有直接参与到技术争议中，但提供了实践中的心得。
• kragen的评论则是对项目文档的命名提出改进建议，未涉及技术细节争议。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源代码的价值与风险，特别是在生成式AI（如LLM）时代下的影响。

不同观点：
• **marssaxman的观点**：支持开源，认为自己的代码无论是直接还是间接被使用都不重要，关键是希望别人能用。
• **Viliam1234的观点**：也支持开源，认为自己从别人那里学到了很多，开源是一种回馈方式。
• **ipaddr的观点**：对开源持怀疑态度。担心在当前LLM生成辅助的背景下，开源项目可能会被他人利用，甚至冒名顶替，从而让原创工作贬值。认为代码的价值正在被削弱。
• **msgodel的观点**：认为ipaddr的观点近乎疯狂，似乎不认同对开源持如此消极的态度。
• **danjl的观点**：对开源持积极态度，认为即便LLM从开源代码中学习并改进，最终也会帮助所有人。提到自己写的大量代码已经消失在历史中，希望它们能被保存下来。
• **throwarayes的观点**：认为即使LLM利用开源代码，也需要付出维护和再创造的努力，门槛较高。对于使用Apache/MIT许可的开源代码，不介意他人从中获取片段。
• **chistev的观点**：对开源持犹豫态度，担心自己正在开发的SAAS项目未来可能盈利。不过也提到如果项目失败，会考虑将其开源以丰富个人作品集。
• **RicoElectrico的观点**：从艺术家角度分析，认为代码和艺术作品一样，其价值主要在于知识和经验。提到历史上创作和复制的难易程度变化，指出在AI时代，创作变得容易，传统创作者谋生的模式受到挑战。
• **bigyabai的观点**：认为代码没有内在价值，除非他人逐字复制并违反许可，否则不算“剽窃”。不担心AI时代下的开源，引用Stallman的观点，认为代码的最大价值在于对他人有实用性，并支持零利润开源软件生产作为最终目标。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：开源代码在AI时代的价值和风险，尤其是LLM可能利用开源代码生成新项目，导致原创作者被忽视或冒名。部分人认为代码的价值在于知识和经验的积累，而另一些人则认为代码应更多地服务于公共利益，即便在AI时代也是如此。
• **对AI影响的看法分歧**：一些人担心AI会削弱代码的独特性和原创性，而另一些人则认为AI能帮助改进代码并造福所有人。
• **开源许可的角色**：讨论中多次提到开源许可的重要性，如Apache/MIT许可，认为这些许可在保护原创作者权益的同时，也促进了代码的共享和使用。

data.title: Sound As Pure Form: Music Language Inspired by Supercollider, APL, and Forth
data.author: mindcrime
data.article_summary: "Sound As Pure Form" (sapf) 是一个用于音频合成的解释器，采用类似Forth的语法，支持懒惰列表和类似APL的自动映射。该语言功能性强、基于栈、使用后缀表示法，旨在通过高层次的函数和自动映射、扫描、归约操作符处理音频和控制事件。sapf受APL、Joy、Haskell等语言启发，强调简洁表达和并发处理能力。其特点包括函数组合自然、无需考虑操作优先级和分隔符、支持多返回值等。虽然受启于连接式编程，但sapf包含词法变量。设置包括将程序放入执行路径、去除苹果的隔离属性、配置环境变量，并可通过命令行运行和查看示例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于新发布的音频编程语言SAPF的评价和讨论

不同观点：
• **pierrec** 认为SAPF的连接式语法虽然初看深奥，但非常适合音频DSP（数字信号处理）的创作，并且其简单的基本概念一旦掌握后使用起来相对容易。他还提到SAPF与Forth-like的音频语言（如Sporth）有相似之处，并提供了相关在线资源。同时，他赞赏SAPF中加入的类似APL的函数元素，并表示有兴趣为SAPF创建WASM构建。

• **spacechild1** 提供了与SAPF相关的资源，包括Supercollider论坛的讨论区链接以及作者James的在线演示视频，并指出SAPF的作者是Supercollider的原作者James McCartney，为不熟悉的人提供了背景信息。

• **chaosprint** 推荐了另一个音乐编程语言Glicol，并提供了相关链接和正在进行的嵌入式系统移植工作，为对音乐编程语言感兴趣的人提供了另一种选择。

• **ssfrr** 对SAPF内置支持Snyderphonics Manta这一小众控制器表示惊讶，并提到自己曾编写libmanta库，该库被SAPF引用，表达了对看到自己作品被应用的喜悦。

• **vanderZwan** 从概念上对SAPF的懒序列处理能力表示赞赏，认为其高层次的函数和自动映射、扫描、归约操作符非常酷，即使不考虑其音乐语言背景。

• **ofalkaed** 对如何在Linux上编译SAPF表示困惑，提到Xcode项目和CoreFoundation.h可能是编译中的障碍，并表示自己缺乏足够的C++知识来解决这一问题。

• **polotics** 表达了对是否应从Supercollider切换到SAPF的犹豫，关注两者之间的集成和重用可能性，提出了是否存在桥梁或兼容方法的问题。

• **ViscountPenguin** 希望有Linux下的二进制版本（如flatpak），提到自己在Ubuntu上尝试其他音乐编程语言时遇到困难，甚至不得不双启动到Windows使用SonicPi。

• **bjt12345** 对SAPF演示中的温暖模拟音色表示好奇，询问其原因。

• **SomeHacker44** 简单指出SAPF似乎是MacOS专属。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是如何在Linux上编译和运行SAPF，反映了对跨平台支持的需求。
• 对SAPF音色的技术细节有好奇，如**bjt12345**对温暖模拟音色的提问。
• 用户在讨论中提供了多个相关资源链接，如SAPF和Glicol的在线演示和代码库，丰富了讨论内容。
• 对于从其他音频编程语言（如Supercollider）切换到SAPF的讨论，体现了用户在选择工具时的实际考虑和犹豫。

WHAT
This program is called:
"A tool for exploring sound as pure form." or "sound as pure form" or "sapf"
It is an interpreter for a language for creating and transforming sound. The
language is mostly functional, stack based and uses postfix notation similar to
FORTH. It represents audio and control events using lazy, possibly infinite
sequences. It intends to do for lazy sequences what APL does for arrays: provide
very high level functions with pervasive automatic mapping, scanning, and
reduction operators. This makes for a language where short programs can achieve
results out of proportion to their size. Because nearly all of the programmer
accessible data types are immutable, the language can easily run multiple
threads without deadlock or corruption.
WHY
Other languages that inspired this one:
APL, Joy[1], Haskell, Piccola[2], Nyquist[3], SuperCollider[4].
APL and FORTH (from which Joy derives) are both widely derided for being
write-only languages. Nevertheless, there has yet to be a language of such
concise expressive power as APL or its descendants. APL is powerful not because
of its bizarre symbols or syntax, but due to the way it automatically maps
operations over arrays and allows iterations at depth within arrays. This means
one almost never needs to write a loop or think about operations one-at-a-time.
Instead one can think about operations on whole structures.
Here is a great quote from Alan Perlis[5] on APL, which that also reflects my
interest in this way of programming :
"What attracted me, then, to APL was a feeling that perhaps through APL one
might begin to acquire some of the dimensions in programming that we revere in
natural language — some of the pleasures of composition; of saying things
elegantly; of being brief, poetic, artistic, that makes our natural languages
so precious to us."
The Joy language introduced concatenative functional programming. This generally
means a stack based virtual machine, and a program consisting of words which are
functions taking an input stack and returning an output stack. The natural
syntax that results is postfix. Over a very long time I have come to feel that
syntax gets in between me and the power in a language. Postfix is the least
syntax possible.
There are several reasons I like the concatenative style of programming:
Function composition is concatenation.
Pipelining values through functions to get new values is the most natural
idiom.
Functions are applied from left to right instead of inside out.
Support for multiple return values comes for free.
No need for operator precedence.
Fewer delimiters are required:
Parentheses are not needed to control operator precedence.
Semicolons are not needed to separate statements.
Commas are not needed to separate arguments.
(Note: Sapf is inspired by, but is not purely a concatenative language because it has lexical variables.)
When I am programming interactively, I most often find myself in the situation
where I have a value and I want to transform it to something else. The thing to
do is apply a function with some parameters. With concatenative programming this
is very natural. You string along several words and get a new value.
QUICK SET-UP
Put the sapf program into ~/bin or wherever you keep commands.
Since this binary is unsigned you will need to remove Apple's quarantine attribute:
xattr -r -d com.apple.quarantine <path-to-sapf-binary>
Set up the environment variables in Terminal or your shell profile.
For example:
export SAPF_HISTORY="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-history.txt"
export SAPF_LOG="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-log.txt"
export SAPF_PRELUDE="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-prelude.txt"
export SAPF_EXAMPLES="$HOME/sapf-files/sapf-examples.txt"
export SAPF_README="$HOME/sapf-files/README.txt"
export SAPF_RECORDINGS="$HOME/sapf-files/recordings"
export SAPF_SPECTROGRAMS="$HOME/sapf-files/spectrograms"
read this README.
check out some examples:
start sapf in Terminal.
open sapf-examples.txt in a text editor
copy an example onto the command line.
COMMAND LINE
sapf [-r sample-rate][-p prelude-file]
sapf [-h]
print this help
OPTIONS
-r sample-rate
Sets the session sample rat

data.title: U.S. has bombed Fordo nuclear plant in attack on Iran
data.author: mattcollins
data.article_summary: 美国轰炸了伊朗的福尔多等核设施，特朗普称此举为“辉煌的军事成功”，并警告伊朗若不寻求和平，将面临更严重打击。伊朗媒体证实福尔多核设施遭到攻击，但未透露具体损失。此次袭击被视为特朗普外交政策的体现，对伊朗与以色列关系产生重大影响。哈马斯谴责美国袭击为“公然侵略”，而以色列则称赞特朗普的“勇敢决定”。专家指出，美国对伊朗核设施造成了重大打击，但具体损毁情况需进一步评估。此次行动引发了对美伊冲突升级的担忧，以及特朗普是否准备推动伊朗政权更迭的猜测。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：伊朗局势及相关国际反应

不同观点：
• 一些评论关注军事行动的直接影响和武器技术，如[tptacek]对GBU-57 "bunker buster"炸弹的描述，以及[ggm]对炸弹历史和伊朗建筑技术的讨论。这些评论聚焦于技术细节和军事能力。
• [neilv]对全球和平的期望与对历史不公的反思形成一种人道主义视角，强调对不公正行为的反思以及对和平的渴望。
• [markus_zhang]和[cedws]关注政治后果和伊朗核计划的未来，质疑这次行动是否会结束伊朗的核野心。
• [greenavocado]从地缘政治角度分析美国、中国和伊朗之间的关系，强调最近的中伊铁路链接对美国全球主导地位的挑战。
• [dkjaudyeqooe]和[duxup]警告军事行动的潜在风险和长期不稳定性，包括中东的不稳定、无休止的战争可能性以及核扩散的威胁。
• [le-mark]将事件归因于内塔尼亚胡对特朗普的影响，并预测中国和俄罗斯会借机扩大影响力，批评特朗普政府的决策能力。
• [vaughands]和[denkmoon]质疑美国行动的实际效益，[vaughands]直接质疑美国的利益所在，[denkmoon]则认为伊朗会因缺乏常规防御能力而追求核武，作为最终威慑手段。
• [Waterluvian]从个人视角反思国际政治，认为某些国家追求核武可能是对国际威胁的合理回应，质疑当今国际政治中的正义立场。

补充讨论：

data.title: Debunking NIST's calculation of the Kyber-512 security level (2023)
data.author: RA2lover
data.article_summary: 这篇文章总结了cr.yp.to博客上的一系列技术主题，涵盖从后量子加密、编译器优化到安全漏洞分析等内容。关键主题包括对Kyber-512算法门计数和NIST计算的分析与反驳，讨论了Turbo Boost技术带来的安全风险，以及对McEliece标准化的展望。此外，文章还涉及量子计算、双重加密、专利延迟推出后量子加密的原因、NSA和NIST的法律诉讼、以及对欧洲量子宣言的批评。技术细节涉及随机数生成器、向量化介绍、ROCA攻击案例研究、以及批量攻击的经济性等。整体内容强调了安全分析、算法优化及其在现实世界中的应用与挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NIST在密码算法选择和计算中的潜在问题，特别是关于Kyber-512和NTRU的讨论，以及对比特币挖矿计算能力的讨论。

不同观点：
• [ggm] 认为NIST在算法选择上可能存在算术错误，且未正式承认或纠正这一问题。他们质疑NIST是否接受了这一错误，并关注NIST是否继续支持Kyber-512而不予解释。
   
• [zzo38computer] 提到了NIST可能存在的其他问题，包括是否有人贿赂或胁迫NIST，以及NIST对算法专利和保密算法的处理。他们还讨论了Kyber和NTRU的区别，指出Kyber是密钥封装机制，而NTRU是公钥加密系统，因此它们不是同一类算法。zzo38computer还提到可以使用多种算法和独立密钥来增强安全性。

• [wahern] 对比特币挖矿的全球计算能力进行了分析，引用数据来验证2022年比特币挖矿的计算量达到了2^111比特操作。他们对比特币挖矿的计算能力增长表示惊讶，并推测全球总计算量可能远远超过比特币挖矿的计算量。

• [perching_aix] 对安全领域中未使用机械化数学证明表示失望，认为这可能导致误解和错误。他们原本期望安全领域中的每一步都经过严格的数学验证。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是NIST是否在算法选择上犯了算术错误，以及是否对外正式承认了这一错误。
• 另一个讨论点是NIST在算法选择过程中是否受到外部压力或影响，以及他们在处理专利和保密算法上的透明度。
• 关于Kyber和NTRU的区别，讨论者提到它们不是同一类算法，因此可能在应用场景和安全性分析上有所不同。
• 比特币挖矿的全球计算能力被用来对比和强调现代计算能力的飞速增长，这一数据引发了对计算资源使用和分配的更广泛讨论。
• 对安全领域中缺乏机械化数学证明的失望反映了部分技术社区对安全验证方法的更高期望。

data.title: Application First – Media over QUIC
data.author: wofo
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己从Discord离职并专注于开发Media over QUIC项目的历程。作者曾在Twitch和Discord工作，尝试通过QUIC和WebTransport解决WebRTC的延迟问题，并创建了Warp项目，但因公司战略变化和标准化的复杂性而受阻。作者认为Media over QUIC在CDN支持方面有潜力，但现有技术如WebRTC、HLS/DASH等已能很好满足当前需求，因此需要找到用户真正关心的应用场景。作者决定成立初创公司，继续推进Media over QUIC，并将通用组件开源。尽管标准化的过程耗时且充满争议，作者仍坚信该技术的未来。

44341138.article_content:
published 5/2/2025
Application First
Today was my last day at Discord.
It’s a great company with a great product and great people.
If you’re an A/V engineer in SF,
take my job
and make me proud.
My brain says I’m making a mistake, but my heart wants to kamikaze into the sun.
It’s time to double down on this passion project.
tl;dr
I’m making a startup to progress Media over QUIC.
Any generic components will be open-source.
It’s going to be sick.
Artistic interpretation of a real mood I swear.
Media over QUIC
But before I explain more, I have to bore you with some history.
I’ve been working on Media over QUIC for a long time.
My fateful project to reduce latency at Twitch was over 5 years ago (!).
We tried using WebRTC, but it just kind of sucked; it wasn’t designed for our use case.
I eventually stumbled upon QUIC/WebTransport and
pivoted once more
.
I built something called Warp as a LL-HLS replacement for Twitch and it was pretty good.
We needed more browser support and somehow had to convince Apple this was worth adding to Safari.
So I got permission to release it as an
IETF draft
despite knowing nothing about standards bodies.
And when I say “permission”, I mean we needed to get Twitch lawyers to fight against Amazon lawyers to participate in the IETF and strike down a provincial patent filed without my knowledge.
FUN TIMES WERE HAD.
Unfortunately, priorities at Twitch changed and Warp was only briefly in production for 10% of Chrome users.
Amazon finally noticed that we were losing a ton of money and the post-Covid downsizing began.
But hey, I got severance and used it to build this crude
quic.video
website while in a coffee shop in Tokyo.
I’m back in San Francisco now; a huge downgrade.
Standardization
It turned out that the Warp draft struck a chord within IETF.
Meta
and
Cisco
had both published similar drafts.
All I had to do was
combine our drafts
and boom, we’d have the start of a new standard.
The
Media over QUIC
working group was born.
It’s apparently the most active working group
with a variety of drafts
aiming to shake up the industry.
However.
HOWEVER.
I decided this was not the most productive path
.
I stopped my involvement, and I’m no longer listed as an author on the
latest moq-transport draft
.
It would have been cool to put
author of RFC9876
on my resume.
Oh well.
Trying to standardize an experimental protocol is just a huge time sink.
Arguing with multiple people from a big established company (
cough
Cisco
cough
) was a nightmare.
I was going nowhere in a hurry.
I decided it would be better to join an existing company, like
Discord
, and see if I couldn’t replace WebRTC from within.
I’m kind of a gamer and have always wanted to work at Discord.
My BFF had just become the boss of the A/V team and I was like “I’m in”.
Well that failed.
I did some neat things at Discord, like rewriting the WebRTC SFU in Rust.
But my primary passion is MoQ and it just didn’t make any product sense.
Why would you rewrite your established A/V stack for nearly zero new features?
Why not fork WebRTC (even more) instead?
Who cares about a “simpler” protocol when everything already “works”?
Discord is prioritizing the right projects and making incremental improvements.
I can’t disagree with any of the decisions and priorities.
Like I said, it’s a great company and I hope one day they’ll end up using MoQ.
But I can’t keep working on WebRTC.
There’s just too many things that I wish I could improve but I’m forced to maintain compatibility with
libwebrtc
for browser support.
It’s a lucrative dead end.
And a bitch.
LET ME OUUUUUT
Strengths First
I’m guilty of advocating for new tech just for the sake of it.
It’s how you push boundaries.
But it’s also how you pivot in a circle.
And boy do I love rewriting stuff.
It might sound obvious, but you need to figure out what a new technology is good at
before
you use it.
It could be significantly faster, or have significantly more features, or be significantly cheaper.
But it has to have
something
.
Otherwise you’re just migrating to the nextest Javacript framework and irritating every coworker in a 5-mile radius.
So what is Media over QUIC good at?
Well, the story around CDN support is great, which is why so many CDN companies are actively participating and building prototypes.
Google, Akamai, Cloudflare, Fastly, etc.
But what real
product
use cases does it solve?
Why would you use it over WebRTC or HLS/DASH or SRT or RTMP or TeamSpeak?
Don’t get me wrong, CDN support is great, but I’m not going to rebuild my entire media stack for that, nor would it be cheaper than existing HTTP and WebRTC CDNs.
I need something users care about.
That’s where the standardization effort falls short.
The working group is focused on dumb shit like reinventing HTTP/1.1 pipelining via
FETCH
.
The motivation is to support VOD, which is noble, but it’s something HLS/DASH (via HTTP) already does very well.
There’s no point reinventing the
<video>
tag.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Harper与Grammarly等其他语法检查工具的对比，以及对自然语言处理（NLP）技术发展历程的讨论。

不同观点：
• **oersted**：认为Harper主要依赖硬编码规则，而非传统的统计NLP方法或LLM（大语言模型）。虽然肯定了Harper的实用性，但指出LLM等新技术正在取代旧有的NLP方法，并认为不应忽视过去的经验和技术。
• **tolerance**：更倾向于使用开源工具，因为规则透明且可修改，相比之下，LLM工具的规则不够透明，可能依赖于训练数据，不如开源工具可控。
• **aDyslecticCrow**：作为长期使用Grammarly的用户，认为Harper在拼写检查方面不如Grammarly，尤其在基于句子上下文建议正确单词方面。虽然Harper比其他工具更接近其需求，但仍偏好Grammarly。
• **shortformblog**：提到另一个开源工具LanguageTool，并指出Harper的竞争对比不完全，因为未提到LanguageTool也可以本地运行。
• **pram**：认为不使用LLM是Harper的优点，批评Grammarly由于加入AI功能而变得 inconsistent（不一致）。
• **demarq**：通过实例指出Harper在语法检查上的不足，认为其规则需要更多贡献才能达到Grammarly的水平。
• **healsdata**：对Automattic的产品持怀疑态度，担心其成功后会因盈利目的而被破坏。
• **icapybara**：支持使用LLM进行语言学习工具，认为LLM在语言处理上表现优异，并反问是否见过ChatGPT犯英语错误。
• **raybb**：希望Harper有一个网站可以测试功能，而不仅是在扩展中使用，因为目前扩展存在问题。
• **loughnane**：提到另一个工具Vale，并询问是否值得转向Harper，表示对Vale的喜爱，但承认Grammarly在某些场景下更具打磨。
• **ErrorNoBrain**：不信任Grammarly，认为其隐私性差，且作为多语言用户使用体验不佳。
• **ibobev**：长期使用Grammarly，尝试Harper后认为其表现不佳，目前不值得使用。
• **krick**：关注Harper是否仅支持英语，询问是否可以扩展到其他语言，或者其框架是否过于英语特定。

补充讨论：
• **LLM与传统NLP方法的争议**：oersted指出LLM取代了传统NLP方法，但认为不应忽视过去的技术积累。icapybara则完全信任LLM，并反问ChatGPT是否犯过英语错误。
• **开源与专有工具的讨论**：tolerance和shortformblog更倾向于使用开源工具，认为规则透明且可控，而专有工具可能隐藏规则或依赖不透明的训练数据。
• **工具的实用性与扩展性**：raybb指出Harper在扩展中的问题，希望有更好的测试途径。krick关注Harper的多语言支持潜力，质疑其框架是否适合扩展到其他语言。

争议焦点：Harper是否能在功能上媲美Grammarly，以及LLM在语言检查工具中的适用性和优势。

data.title: Developing a Retro-Roguelike Game for Multiple Platforms in C
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了开发一款可在多种 vintage 和现代计算机上运行的复古 Roguelike 游戏的过程和挑战。作者最初使用 TRSE 开发环境尝试跨平台编译，但遇到了诸如 Pascal 不熟悉、文本支持不一致和 ASCII 字符映射差异等问题。随后，作者转向使用 C 语言，利用其广泛的编译器支持和低级硬件控制能力，通过条件编译来处理不同系统的差异。然而，C 语言开发也面临编译器差异和代码膨胀等问题。最终，作者决定专注于支持具备 64K 以上内存的系统，如 Commodore 64、Atari 800 和 CP/M 系统，同时包括现代平台如 Linux、Mac 和 Windows。游戏核心包括程序生成的地图，以确保每次游戏体验独特，同时节省手动绘制地图的工作。

Retro Game Coders Blog

Developing a Retro-Roguelike Game for Multiple Platforms in C
Creating a game that runs smoothly across different vintage and modern computers is a complex and ambitious challenge. Can I achieve it?
Let me tell you the story so far; the process, obstacles, and solutions involved in making a roguelike dungeon crawler playable on systems like the Commodore 64, Commodore PET, and even more constrained machines.
Watch on
YouTube
Why Build Games for Multiple Platforms?
Many enthusiasts collect old computers just for their nostalgic value. However, having these hardware collections provide playable experiences affords fresh ways to enjoy and preserve their unique quirks and capabilities.
My goal was to develop a game that can run on, if not
all,
then at least across numerous systems, utilising each machine’s features while managing constraints like memory, graphics, and input methods.
First Approach: Using TRSE to Compile for Multiple Target Systems
The journey began with
TRSE
, a development environment supporting a huge number of vintage computer systems. My plan was to develop a text-based roguelike that could run on various hardware by compiling code for each target.
Problems
TRSE is broadly based on Pascal, unfamiliar territory for me, especially when I take long breaks from the environment.
Many older computers had incomplete or inconsistent text support in TRSE libraries as most people in the community generally develop for each systems
graphics
hardware.
Differences in hardware standards like ASCII character mapping caused compatibility headaches, especially on pre-1980s machines.
Lessons Learned
Multiplatform development on vintage hardware is additionally complicated compared to today because system standards and capabilities vary widely, even from the same company, using the same processor.
Support libraries are not always fully fleshed out in ways that match your vision, or might need adaptation for different systems.
TRSE is an amazing and pretty recent voluntary project so support for certain machines needs to come from the community.
Transitioning to C for Greater Opportunity
Realising my limitations from choosing TRSE, I shifted towards programming in C. Since C compilers exist for a broad array of hardware, from calculators to mainframes, my hope was to create a universal codebase.
Anticipated benefits of C:
Wide availability of cross-compiler support.
I had experience writing portable code adaptable to multiple hardware environments.
Features for control over low-level hardware interactions when required.
Reality Check
Despite C’s portability, a fair amount of conditional code must be used to accommodate different system architectures.
Variations in compilers (e.g., CC65, Z88DK) and variable adherence to standards (C89, C99) introduce added complexity.
Managing Platform Differences Through Conditional Compilation
One of the key techniques I used was
conditional compilation
. This process involves including or excluding parts of the code depending on the target system.
Example:
#ifdef C64
// Specific code for Commodore 64
#endif
#ifdef PET
// Specific code for Commodore PET
#endif
However, this approach becomes demanding because:
Different compilers have varying syntax and features.
Each system’s memory and graphics capabilities differ.
Code can become bloated and hard to maintain.
My focus shifted from
balancing the effort needed to support many platforms versus focusing on one.
The Challenge of Hardware Limitations
Supporting multiple machines means accounting for:
Memory constraints:
e.g., I currently have a minimum 48K RAM limit, though I would love to address this for my beloved Vic 20 by utilising RAM upgrade cartridge support.
Graphics and character sets:
Some systems have custom character graphics, others don’t.
Input controls:
Many vintage machines used keyboards, not all had native joystick support.
Loading mechanisms:
From tapes to disks, resource management varies.
All this complexity led to a strategy of focusing on systems with similar capabilities , mainly those with
64K RAM or more
, such as:
Commodore 64, PET, Plus+4, Atari 800, BBC Micro
CP/M-based systems such as IMSAI and Altair
Linux, Mac, Windows (via terminal and a graphical version using Raylib)
Developing the Core Game: Levels, Map Generation, and Graphics
Hand-Crafted Dungeons to Random Map Generation
A big win was creating a
procedurally generated map
to make each gameplay experience unique and to save me having the added task of hand drawing maps in a level editor. The main downside is the ram this process takes up versus loading a complete map on level change. Fortunately, the delay for generating the map is not as long as I feared so it is not a very noticeable pause in action.
This map generator produces random but walkable layouts, and based on guard-rails in the logic, adds the baddies and collectibles throughout the level.
That meant at this point the game included:

data.title: The Tandy Corporation, Part 1 – By Bradford Morgan White
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 《Tandy Corporation, Part 1》一文讲述了Tandy公司的起源与早期发展。1919年，David Lewis Tandy和Norton Hinckley创立了Hinckley-Tandy皮革公司，专营皮革制品。Tandy家族专注销售和市场，公司逐渐扩展。David的儿子Charles David Tandy在二战后创立了Tandy Leather业余爱好部门，通过邮购业务取得成功。由于经营理念分歧，Tandy家族最终掌控公司，并于1950年代快速扩展零售业务。1954年，David去世后，公司因遗产税陷入财务困境，Charles通过与一家上市公司合并解决这一问题，并最终在1959年重新掌控公司，将其更名为Tandy Corporation。之后，公司股票上市，并开始多元化经营，包括电子产品，推动公司进一步增长。

In 1919, a small leather company was founded in Fort Worth by David Lewis Tandy and Norton Hinckley. The Hinckley-Tandy Leather Company specialized in leather show laces, shoe soles, leather and rubber heels, and other shoe-findings. Tandy focused on sales and marketing while Hinckley managed the internal business operations and inventory. The company did well, bought a larger location in 1923 and expanded to Beaumont in 1927. The company scaled back during the Depression, but they survived.
Charles David Tandy
Charles David Tandy, the son of David Lewis Tandy, was born a year before Hinckley-Tandy started operations, and he began working at the company at the age of twelve. He graduated from Texas Christian University in 1940, briefly attended the Harvard Business School, and he then joined the US Navy. The younger Tandy served as a supply officer, but he also setup a leather working program for hospitalized personnel. This was successful, and it provided the inspiration for his first major contribution to Hinckley-Tandy after his discharge in 1948: Tandy Leather, a mail order hobby division of the company.
Disagreements between Hinckley and the Tandys were growing. Hinckley wanted to focus on the shoe-findings that had built the company, while the Tandys had greater ambitions. The Tandy family ended up in control of the company and the hobby division had achieved 100% ROI in its first year. In May of 1950, Charles Tandy opened the first two retail locations specialized in leather craft, but the company’s main revenues came from their mail order business. At two years, the company had achieved $2.9 million in sales, opened 15 stores, and wasn’t yet ready to stop its expansion. By 1952, the company had stores across the country, had acquired a few failing competitors, and had established an interesting method of encouraging both employees and store managers to succeed. Each store was incorporated individually, and store managers were required to own a 25% stake in the store. Should a manager lack the capital personally, Tandy Leather was available to provide the loan for that purpose, and Dave Tandy would serve as a co-signer should it be needed. For regular employees across the company, year end bonuses were provided, and all staff were eligible and encouraged to purchase equity. This worked well; by 1954, the company’s catalog was 68 pages and served a million customers, four factories stocked the shelves of 67 stores spread across 36 states and the territory of Hawaii.
While one might assume that taxation would require respiration, this is not so. In 1954, Dave Tandy passed away and the estate taxes hurt the company’s finances rather badly. This sudden shift in the company’s fortunes also meant that employee stock holders had no meaningful way to assess the value of their shares. As the remaining Tandy in our story saw it, the easiest way to ameliorate the concerns of share holders was for the company to go public. Given the company’s size, this would have been difficult, and he therefore sought a merger with an already publicly listed company.
The merger target Tandy found was the American Hide and Leather Company. AHLC was insolvent and this presented Tandy with the chance to remain in control of the resulting conglomerate. Tandy Leather provided AHLC the money to buy Tandy Leather, and Tandy Leather share holders had the option to buy shares in AHLC. This merger was completed in 1955, the company was renamed to General American Industries Inc, Tandy became the president, and the combined entity had a five year tax shelter due to AHLC’s insolvency. With AHLC as the corporate parent, profits from Tandy Leather were being used to cover the losses of other conglomerate members such as Western Leather and Tex Tan. To stop this would mean that Tandy would need to regain control. This was achieved in November of 1959.
With Tandy now in control, the unprofitable child companies were sold at a loss, the company’s headquarters was moved to Fort Worth, the conglomerate was renamed the Tandy Corporation, and the stock symbol became TAN. At open the stock was $4/share, and by the end of 1961 it was $11/share.
With ownership, earnings, taxes, and other issues settled, Tandy changed his focus back to growth. The first two initiatives were experimental retail stores Tandy Craft and Hobby Mart in November of 1961. The first stores were around 18,000 square feet, sold more than 50,000 items of varying kinds for a variety of hobbies, and notably included Electronic Crafts like DIY radio and stereo kits. Other diversification efforts continued over the decade with names like The Mart, and Pier 1 Imports.
Two years after the founding of Hin

data.author: diggan
data.article_summary:
本文简要介绍了Arma 3在2.20更新中对多线程处理的优化，旨在提升游戏流畅度，减少卡顿和帧率波动。虽然RV引擎自Arma 2以来一直支持多线程，但此次更新对其进行了全面改进，特别关注于减少lag spike和提升最低FPS，使游戏感觉更加顺畅。更新后，最高FPS可能变化不大，甚至在超高帧率下可能略有下降，但整体游戏体验更加平滑。

文章还提到玩家在使用Profiling分支测试时因错误命令行参数导致问题，建议玩家正确设置参数，避免不必要的性能影响。例如，不需要手动设置-cpuCount来限制CPU核心数，-enableHT参数效果因硬件而异，而-exThreads参数不应使用。此次优化基于开发团队的深入研究，感谢社区的反馈和支持。

主要讨论点：游戏开发中的并行化、多线程设计及性能优化问题

不同观点：
• **[o11c]** 认为AI和脚本无法并行化的常见问题源于设计选择，即所有角色都拥有全局对象的准确信息。如果每个角色仅保存自己所需的世界信息副本，就可以实现并行化，虽然这会增加内存使用，但可以通过限制副本大小来控制。此外，建议不要在脚本API中暴露隐式访问状态的函数，而是通过显式传递对象来控制访问和修改权限，这样可以提高设计的清晰度和可维护性。

• **[egypturnash]** 提到了玩家因过时优化指南设置错误命令行参数，导致游戏多线程优化后出现问题。建议可以增加弹窗提示，警告玩家某些参数可能不再适用，并引导他们查看相关博客以获取更多信息，从而避免错误设置影响游戏体验。

• **[hinkley]** 讨论了作业系统设计对多线程利用的影响，指出旧的设计存在局限性，比如所有任务必须一次性提交并等待完成，导致效率低下（即"Fork-Join"模式）。通过改造系统，允许任务以队列形式持续运行，能够显著提升吞吐量，并且解决了某些任务集群造成的负载问题。此外，强调了突发高负载对系统的影响，建议通过自我限制流量来避免内存压力，并给自动扩展系统留出适应时间。

补充讨论：
• **[abrookewood]** 和 **[absurdo]** 的评论主要表达了对老游戏《Operation Flashpoint: Cold War Crisis》的怀旧和赞赏，认为其在军事模拟游戏中仍然表现出色，并对长期更新表示惊讶和认可。这些评论并未直接涉及技术讨论，而是对游戏本身的历史和质量进行了评价。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在如何有效实现AI和脚本的并行化（[o11c]的观点），以及多线程系统设计中的具体优化策略（[hinkley]的实际案例分享）。这些讨论反映出在游戏开发中，如何在保证性能的同时实现合理的设计和优化是开发者们关注的重点。

44303246.article_content:
reported by
Dedmen
on June 17, 2025
UNIT
: Dedmen, Programmer, Programming
TO
: Arma 3 Users
OPSUM
: An analysis of recent multithreading improvements for a smoother game experience
SITREP
Welcome to this technical deep dive into
Arma 3
's performance optimizations in
update 2.20
. Before handing you over to this blog's actual author, I wanted to share a few words on the state of Live Ops. Yes, REPception is now a thing.
Some 12 years since its initial release, we still find ourselves releasing free platform updates to the game. This is something we can hardly believe ourselves, and we think you'll agree that it's a splendid situation! Thanks to the continued support from the game's community and Bohemia Interactive leadership, we're still in a position to offer some limited Live Ops development. The hands-on team can be counted on one hand now, but we should not forget it takes a bigger support network to keep things flowing smoothly. Publishing, Quality Assurance, Localization, Legal, IT, and more teams and individuals have a hand in getting these updates out. Meanwhile, some of our longer-term plans, as outlined in
older SITREPs
, are still on our list. Their roll-out has been slower than anticipated, but that's in part due to it just not being necessary to switch to the next phase of Arma 3's life cycle. Even now that we're steadily traveling the road towards
Arma 4
, there is still plenty of life left in our pinnacle
Real Virtuality
(RV) title.
Those of you who are on our
Discord server
(
#perf_prof_branch
channel) may have been following along with the optimizations now released to main branch in 2.20. You may have already enjoyed Programmer
"Dedmen"
's incredible monologues on specific issues, solutions, fixes, and a myriad of other RV topics. You may have also wondered why these optimizations only arrive now. There are many reasons for that, some of which Dedmen will outline below. It's hard to compare the prime-time development circumstances a decade ago to how things are now. There are effectively no hard deadlines for Arma 3 anymore, so there is ample time to investigate and experiment. There also aren't hundreds of commits from tens of people every day, with a constant stream of new features arriving and bugs being squashed. We are building upon the work of legends, going all the way back to the first lines of code for RV by
Ondřej Španěl
.
Nonetheless, I want to give massive kudos to the incredible work by our talented Dedmen. He has accomplished low-level and risky changes that I would have never anticipated at this stage. They will not magically give everyone the same performance boost across the board, but don't just stare blindly at the numbers. Play the game. Most everyone who's tried the update has said the game feels smoother. Thank you for the passionate and hard work, Dedmen. And a big thanks to everybody who has helped us test these changes via
Profiling branch
as well. Your feedback has been very important in testing under real-world conditions.
Enough from me, let's finally get to the meat of this Operations Report.
- Joris-Jan van 't Land, Project Lead
FRAMES
First of all,
we did not "add" multithreading in update 2.20
. The RV engine has had multithreading since
Arma 2
. But
we did overhaul all of our multithreading code
and made some optimizations that are further detailed below.
The main focus of our optimizations was to fix lag spikes and raise the minimum Frames per Second (FPS). The maximum FPS may not actually be noticeably higher, and in some cases (at above 100 FPS) it may even be slightly lower than before. But the gameplay should still
feel significantly smoother
.
This is also visible in these graphs recorded using
CapFrameX
on the excellent
Yet Another Arma Benchmark
(YAAB)
by
Sams
. The frame times should feel more consistent, with fewer spikes:
The average FPS, meanwhile, has only received a minor bump. And that bump is expected to be even less when mods get involved.
COMMAND-LINEAGE
From the feedback on Profiling branch we have seen several times that players had issues caused by setting
wrong
command-line parameters
. That was typically because an old optimization guide told them it would make their game run better. But now that the game is more multithreaded than it used to be, bad settings have a more noticeable and potentially negative impact.
If you are setting custom parameters, please verify that you understand them and you are setting them correctly. Here are some guidelines:
Only use the
-cpuCount
parameter if you want to intentionally limit how many CPU cores the game can use. The engine can already automatically detect how many cores you have, so you do not need to tell it that.
The
-enableHT
parameter has no effect if -cpuCount is set, so setting both is wrong. Our tests have shown that -enableHT performs worse, but it may depend on your hardware. You can use
YAAB
to test if it actually helps in your case.
The
-exThreads
parameter should not be used. If

data.title: AMD's Freshly-Baked MI350: An Interview with the Chief Architect
data.author: pella
data.article_summary: 在AMD的2025年Advancing AI大会上，首席架构师Alan Smith介绍了最新的MI350系列加速器。MI350基于GFX9（Vega架构），之所以继续使用GFX9，是因为其在分布式计算算法和高性能计算及AI方面的优化已非常成熟。尽管GCN架构有独立的L1缓存和本地数据存储（LDS），MI350通过增加LDS容量至160KB和提升带宽来提升性能。MI350还引入了微缩格式支持，特别是FP6和FP4数据类型，且FP6的处理速度与FP4相同，以提高AI训练和推理效率。此外，MI350未硬件加速支持TF32，因其被BF16取代，后者在吞吐量上更具优势。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AMD MI350系列的硬件性能、市场定位及其与竞争对手Nvidia的比较

不同观点：
• Pella的观点：Pella解释了MI350在FP6数据路径上的设计决策，强调了其在性能上的领先地位，尤其是相对于市场上其他产品的竞争优势。通过增加硬件来实现FP6和FP4数据路径的相同吞吐量，并且在功耗和面积上保持高效。

• Behnamoh的观点：Behnamoh关注MI300和MI350在市场上的供应问题，指出它们仅以x8批次在服务器机架中销售，导致其选择了Nvidia的RTX Pro 6000用于研究。这反映了对单个产品可得性的需求。

• Teleforce的观点：Teleforce对MI350的硬件规格表示赞赏，特别是其拥有2304 GB HMB3E显存的配置，强调了其在高性能计算中的潜在应用。

• Latchkey的观点：Latchkey表示对MI300x的满意，并期待部署MI355，显示了对AMD未来产品的积极期待和信心。

• Jonfromsf的观点：Jonfromsf认为Nvidia的优势不仅仅在于硬件，更在于其软件生态系统。即使有更好的硬件，AMD也需要在软件方面努力才能真正与Nvidia竞争。

• AbuAssar的观点：AbuAssar提出了关于MI350使用的CDNA架构及其与GCN（VEGA）的关系，并猜测未来的MI400是否会跳过GCN直接采用RDNA 5等效架构，反映了用户对AMD未来技术路线的关注。

• Deadbabe的观点：Deadbabe直接质疑AMD是否能够赶上Nvidia，这是对AMD整体竞争力的疑问，特别是在与Nvidia的对比中。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了AMD在硬件设计上的创新（如FP6数据路径）以及其在市场上的定位和供应策略。
• 软件生态系统在竞争中的重要性被提及，特别是与Nvidia的对比中，AMD在软件支持方面的不足被认为是其竞争劣势。
• 对未来产品的预期和架构发展的猜测显示了用户对AMD技术路线图的关注。

Hello you fine Internet folks,
At AMD's Advancing AI 2025, I had the pleasure of interviewing Alan Smith, AMD Senior Fellow and Chief Instinct Architect, about CDNA4 found in the MI350 series of accelerators.
Hope y'all enjoy!
Transcript below has been edited for conciseness and readability.
George:
Hello you fine internet folks! We're here today at AMD's Advancing AI 2025 event, where the MI350 series has just been announced. And I have the pleasure to introduce, Alan Smith from AMD.
Alan:
Hello, everyone.
George:
What do you do at AMD?
Alan
: So I'm the chief architect of Instinct GPUs.
George
: Awesome, what does that job entail?
Alan
: So I'm responsible for the GPU product line definition, working with our data center GPU business partners to define the-, work with them on the definition of the requirements of the GPUs, and then work with the design teams to implement those requirements.
George:
Awesome. So, moving into MI350: MI350's still GFX9 based, and- for you guys in the audience, GFX9 is also known as Vega, or at least derivative of GFX9. Why is it that MI350 is still on GFX9, whereas clients such as RDNA 3 and 4, GFX11 and 12 respectively?
Alan:
Sure, yeah, it's a great question. So as you know, the CDNA architecture off of, you know, previous generations of Instinct GPUs, starting with MI100 and before, like you said, in the Vega generations, were all GCN architecture, which was Graphics Core Next. And over several generations, CDNA's been highly optimized for the types of distributed computing algorithms for high-performance computing and AI. And so we felt like starting with that base for MI350 would give us the right pieces that we needed to deliver the performance goals that we had for the MI350 series.
George:
And with GCN, as you know, there's a separate L1 cache and LDS, or Local Data Store. Why is that still in MI350? And why haven't they been merged?
Alan:
Yeah, so like you said, you know, it is a legacy piece of the GCN architecture. It's sort of fundamental to the way the compute unit is built. So we felt like in this generation, it wasn't the right opportunity to make a microarchitectural change of that scale. So what we did instead, was we increased the capacity of the LDS. So previously in MI300 series, we had a 64 kilobyte LDS, and we've increased that capacity to 160 kilobytes in MI350 series. And in addition to that, we increased the bandwidth as well. So we doubled the bandwidth of the LDS into the register file, in order to be able to feed the Tensor Core rates that we have in the MI350 series.
George:
And speaking of Tensor Cores, you've now introduced microscaling formats to MI350x for FP8, FP6, and FP4 data types. Interestingly enough, a major differentiator for MI350 is that FP6 is the same rate as FP4. Can you talk a little bit about how that was accomplished and why that is?
Alan:
Sure, yep, so one of the things that we felt like on MI350 in this timeframe, that it's going into the market and the current state of AI... we felt like that FP6 is a format that has potential to not only be used for inferencing, but potentially for training. And so we wanted to make sure that the capabilities for FP6 were class-leading relative to... what others maybe would have been implementing, or have implemented. And so, as you know, it's a long lead time to design hardware, so we were thinking about this years ago and wanted to make sure that MI350 had leadership in FP6 performance. So we made a decision to implement the FP6 data path at the same throughput as the FP4 data path. Of course, we had to take on a little bit more hardware in order to do that. FP6 has a few more bits, obviously, that's why it's called FP6. But we were able to do that within the area of constraints that we had in the matrix engine, and do that in a very power- and area-efficient way.
George:
And speaking of data types, I've noticed that TF32 is not on your ops list for hardware level acceleration. Why remove that feature from... or why was that not a major consideration for MI350?
Alan:
Yeah, well, it was a consideration, right? Because we did remove it. We felt like that in this timeframe, that brain float 16, or BF16, would be a format that would be leverageable for most models to replace TF32. And we can deliver a much higher throughput on BF16 than TF32, so we felt like it was the right trade off for this implementation.
George:
And if I was to use TF32, what would the speed be? Would it still be FP32, the speed of FP32?
Alan:
You have a choice. We offer some emulation, and I don't have all the details on the exact throughputs off the top

主要讨论点： elliptic curves 的视觉化呈现及其应用和艺术价值

不同观点：
• **欣赏与喜爱**：
  - **tempodox**: 认为这些视觉化呈现像物理对象，并提议可以3D打印，表示非常有兴趣购买。
  - **cosmodev**: 从专业角度出发，表示自己长期研究zk证明和椭圆曲线，看到这些视觉化呈现感到非常享受，认为这是真正的“极客艺术”。
  - **ykonstant**: 原本预期会失望，但发现这些视觉化不仅美观而且实用，尤其在几何特性保留方面，并推荐了相关论文。
  - **aanet**: 简单表达了对这些视觉化呈现的喜爱，认为非常漂亮。
  - **gloosx**: 将这些视觉化与自然界中的椭圆曲线联系起来，认为它们像花一样能吸引注意力。

• **艺术与创作工具的联想**：
  - **larodi**: 将这些视觉化与Structure Synth和Context Free Art等工具产生的艺术效果联系起来，提出可能存在的数学关联。
  - **matcha-video**: 提到程序化艺术在区块链上的发展，并推荐了艺术家Tyler Hobbs的作品。

• **幽默与实际应用的建议**：
  - **felineflock**: 开玩笑说想把这些图案印在T恤上，但担心被误认为外星甜甜圈店的品牌。
  - **6510**: 幽默地建议可以将这些图案做成饼干卖给数学家。

• **技术与实现细节的关注**：
  - **charlieyu1**: 对如何在有限域上绘制椭圆曲线表示疑惑，指出有限域应该是离散的。
  - **loxias**: 对这些视觉化是否使用Blender渲染表示好奇。

• **请求资源与进一步发展**：
  - **Datagenerator**: 请求分享这些美丽图片的资源，希望能自行重现。
  - **bedit**: 对这些视觉化将抽象数学转化为艺术表示赞赏，并期待网站的进一步发展。

补充讨论：
- 视觉化呈现不仅在数学研究中有价值，也被视为一种艺术形式，引发了关于其工具、技术和实际应用的讨论。
- 部分评论者对视觉化背后的技术细节和实现方法表示关注，希望获取更多资源和信息。
- 幽默和创意应用的建议增加了讨论的趣味性，如T恤和饼干的提议。

data.title: Honda conducts successful launch and landing of experimental reusable rocket
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 2025年6月17日，本田研发公司成功进行了自主研发的可重复使用火箭（长6.3米，直径85厘米，干重900公斤，湿重1,312公斤）的发射和着陆测试。火箭在日本北海道大树町的本田设施发射，达到271.4米的 altitude 后，精准降落在距离目标点37厘米范围内，飞行时长56.6秒。此次测试验证了火箭在上升和下降过程中的飞行稳定性及着陆能力，为实现关键的可重复使用技术奠定了基础。本田自2024年起在大树町进行了多次安全测试，并采取了严格的安全措施，包括设立限制区域和部署安全人员。本田希望通过火箭技术研究，利用其在燃烧和控制技术方面的核心优势，为人们日常生活创造更多价值，并满足未来卫星发射需求的增长。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Honda公司的小型火箭发射及其在航天领域的潜力，以及技术创新与竞争。

不同观点：
• 一些评论对Honda进入航天领域感到意外，但对该公司的工程能力和创新潜力表示赞赏。例如，[Daisywh]认为Honda的工程背景可能正是当前太空探索所需要的，而[EvanAnderson]则通过个人经历强调Honda硬件的可靠性，表达了对Honda未来太空项目的期待。

• 另一部分评论则对Honda的小型火箭技术持保留态度。[leesec]认为尽管为Honda的成就感到高兴，但觉得该公司距离实际应用还有很长的路要走，且相比其他公司已经落后十年以上。

• [ItCouldBeWorse]提到“先锋效应”，认为一旦某项技术被证明可行，其他公司会迅速跟进并找到更高效的解决方案。该评论还指出，有些技术“突破”其实是市场营销的结果，而非真正的技术创新。

• [JoeAltmaier]持较为中立的立场，认为在成熟的空间发射经济中，各种规模和能力的火箭都有其存在的价值，不应低估任何一种火箭的潜力。

补充讨论：
• 技术细节和对比：[robszumski]提供了Rocket Lab的Electron火箭与Honda火箭的湿质量对比，指出Honda火箭小得多。[_joel]则提到了BPS.space的固体燃料推力矢量控制技术，并将其与Honda的成就联系起来。

• 关于公司顶级域名（TLD）的讨论：[kapildev]对公司拥有自己顶级域名（如`.honda`）表示好奇，并质疑为何ICANN允许这种TLD存在。[ghxst]则对`.honda`作为TLD表示赞赏。

• 争议焦点：Honda在航天技术上的创新是否真正具有突破性，或者只是市场营销策略的一部分。这反映了技术进步与市场宣传之间的张力。

• 竞争与行业影响：[walterbell]和[methuselah_in]都提到Honda进入航天领域对行业竞争的积极影响，认为更多的竞争将推动未来的创新。

Jun 17, 2025
Topics
Honda Conducts Successful Launch and Landing Test of Experimental Reusable Rocket
TOKYO, Japan, June 17, 2025 â Honda R&D Co., Ltd., a research and development subsidiary of Honda Motor Co., Ltd., today conducted a launch and landing test of an experimental reusable rocket
*1
(6.3 m in length, 85 cm in diameter, 900 kg dry weight/1,312 kg wet weight) developed independently by Honda. The test was completed successfully, the first time Honda landed a rocket after reaching an altitude of nearly 300 meters.
This test marked the first launch and landing test conducted by Honda with an aim to demonstrate key technologies essential for rocket reusability, such as flight stability during ascent and descent, as well as landing capability. Through this successful test, Honda achieved its intended rocket behaviors for the launch and landing (reaching an altitude of 271.4 m, and landing within 37cm of the target touchdown point, with a flight duration of 56.6 sec), while obtaining data during the ascent and descent.
ï¼Overview of launch and landing test of a Honda reusable rocketï¼
ã»Purpose:Â Â Â Â  Establishment of key technologies necessary for a reusable rocket
ã»Location:Â Â Â Â  Honda facility in Taiki Town
*2
, Hiroo District, Hokkaido Prefecture, Japan
ã»Date/Time:Â  June 17, 2025. Launch time: 16:15
Test being conducted in Taiki Town in Hokkaido, Japan(Photo taken in May, 2025)
Launch and landing test
*1 A reusable rocket, also known as a reusable launch vehicle (RLV), is a type of rocket that, unlike a conventional expendable launch vehicle (ELV), can be used repeatedly in a short period of time. A reusable rocket is launched in a vertical position, reaches an altitude of around 100 kilometers, and then lands back on earth while maintaining a vertical position.
*2 Taiki Town, located in southeastern Hokkaido, Japan, has been developing itself as a âspace townâ through the joint efforts of public and private sectors, and various aviation/space related tests are being conducted by a wide range of organizations including JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency), businesses and universities.
ï¼Safety measures for Honda rocket testingï¼
Since 2024, Honda has been safely conducting engine combustion tests and hovering tests for its reusable rockets in Taiki Town in Hiroo District, Hokkaido, Japan. As with all previous tests, Honda conducted this launch and landing test while placing the highest priority on safety and with the understanding and cooperation of local authorities and residents.Â
Specific safety measures taken for this test
A restricted area with a 1-kilometer radius was established. During the test, access to the area was restricted through the installation of signs and gates, as well as the deployment of security personnel.
The restricted area was defined by calculating the potential area where the rocket could fall to earth in the event of a thrust cut-off and by adding a sufficient buffer zone (safe distance calculated based on the guidelines set forth by the Cabinet Office of the Government of Japan) that would cover the potential area where a blast wave, debris dispersion, or fireballs could impact in the event of an explosion within the potential fall area.
The experimental rocket was equipped with a safety system to prevent deviation from a pre-defined flight corridor, speed and attitude conditions, ensuring no impact beyond the restricted area.
ï¼Honda initiatives in the areas of rocket researchï¼
As announced in 2021, Honda has been pursuing research and development in the field of space technologies while viewing it as a place to take on challenges to realize the âdreamsâ and âpotentialâ of people worldwide while leveraging its core technologies. Honda has the aim to enable people to transcend the constraints of time, place or ability and make peopleâs daily lives more enjoyable. Examples of Honda initiatives toward creating new value in the ultimate environment of outer space include research into a circulative renewable energy system, key robotic technologies for use in outer space and reusable rockets.Â
Inspired by the dream of young Honda engineers who wanted to build rockets by utilizing core technologies amassed by Honda through the development of various products, such as combustion and control technologies, Honda started rocket research based on the belief that it has the potential to contribute more to peopleâs daily lives by launching satellites with its own rockets, that could lead to various services
*3
that are also compatible with other Honda business.
In todayâs world, vast amounts of data are consumed, with the growing expectation for greater utilization of a data system in outer space through expanded use of satellites. In light of this trend, the need for satellite launch rockets is also expected to increase in the coming years.

data.author: birdman3131
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了YouTube相关的一些信息和功能。内容包括YouTube的版权声明、联系方式、创作者相关信息、广告、开发者政策以及使用条款。此外，还提到隐私政策、安全措施、新功能测试、NFL Sunday Ticket等服务，以及YouTube所属的公司信息和版权年份（2025年，Google LLC）。文章主要为用户提供有关YouTube平台的各类重要信息和资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Behringer X32产品的质量及其技术背景（包括开源项目）

不同观点：
• [birdman3131] 提供了一个YouTube视频链接，并提到该视频展示了让Behringer X32运行起来的必要工作。同时，他还分享了相关的GitHub链接，为不想观看视频的人提供了文字资料。这表明他支持通过开源项目（如OpenX32）来增强设备功能，并为不同偏好的人提供了多样的资源。

• [ww520] 高度评价Behringer X32，认为它在设计和构建上都非常出色。他指出该产品的数字和模拟部分、用户界面（包括硬件和软件）、布局、速度以及远程控制功能等各方面都配合得非常好。他还提到产品给他的印象是“由黑客构建的”，并对其由Linux驱动表示赞赏。这显示出他对该产品的技术实现及其开源背景的认同和赞赏。

补充讨论：
• 两者都对Behringer X32的技术背景表示兴趣，[birdman3131] 强调了开源社区的贡献，提供了GitHub链接以供参考，而 [ww520] 则从使用体验的角度，称赞了产品的整体设计和功能。

• [ww520] 的评论中提到“由黑客构建的”这一表述，可能暗示了他对产品设计灵活性和技术深度的欣赏，也可能意味着他对开源社区或技术爱好者对该产品所作贡献的认同。

争议焦点：
• 评论之间并没有明显的争议，但隐含的讨论点在于对产品技术背景的关注角度不同。 [birdman3131] 更关注开源项目的实际操作和技术细节，而 [ww520] 则从用户体验的角度出发，赞赏产品的整体设计和功能实现。

总结来看，两位评论者都对Behringer X32产品的技术背景表示认可，只是关注的细节和角度有所不同。

data.author: transpute
data.article_summary:
本文简要介绍了谷歌TPU（Tensor Processing Units）的设计理念和内部结构，强调其可扩展性、高吞吐量和能效。TPU是谷歌为满足人工智能计算需求而开发的专用集成电路（ASIC），特别擅长处理大规模矩阵乘法和神经网络计算。TPU的强大性能得益于硬件（如能量效率和模块化设计）和软件（如XLA编译器）的协同设计。

TPU的单芯片包含两个TensorCore，每个TensorCore具有共享内存和专门的计算单元，如矩阵乘法单元（MXU）、向量单元（VPU）等。TPU采用脉动阵列设计，通过流水线技术实现高吞吐量，特别适合矩阵乘法和卷积操作。然而，脉动阵列对稀疏矩阵的处理效率较低。

相较于GPU，TPU拥有更大的片上内存和更少的计算核心，但通过优化设计实现了极高的计算效率。例如，TPUv5p单芯片可达500 TFLOPs/秒，而TPUv7整个计算单元可达42.5 ExaFLOPs/秒。

总体而言，TPU通过独特的设计选择，在处理AI任务上展现了出色的性能和能效。

44342977.article_content:
I've been working with TPUs a lot recently and it's fun to see how they had such different design philosophies compared to GPUs.
The main strongpoint for TPUs is in their scalability. This is achieved through a co-design of both the hardware side (e.g. energy efficiency and modularity) and the software side (e.g. XLA compiler).
Background
To give a brief tldr on TPUs, it's
Google's ASIC that focuses on two factors: extreme matmul throughput + energy efficiency.
Their origins go back to Google in 2006, when they were first evaluating whether they should implement either GPUs, FPGAs, or custom ASICs. Back then there were only a few applications that necessitated specialized hardware and they decided those needs could be met by bringing in excess CPU compute from their large datacenters. But this changed in 2013 when Google's voice search feature ran on neural networks and internal projections speculated that they would need much more compute if it took off.
Fast forward to today and TPUs power the majority of Google's AI services. Of course, that includes training and inference of Gemini or Veo, but also deploying their recommendation models (DLRMs).
Let's dive in and look at TPU internals from the bottom up.
TPU Single-Chip Level
I'll focus my diagrams to TPUv4, but this layout is more or less applicable to latest generation TPUs (e.g. TPUv6p "Trillium"; TPUv7 "Ironwood's details aren't released as of writing in June, 2025).
Here's the layout of a single TPUv4 chip:
TPU Single Chip + TensorCore
In each chip, there's two TPU TensorCores, which are responsible for our compute. (Note: inference-specialized TPUs have only one TensorCore). Both TensorCores have shared memory units: CMEM(128MiB) and HBM(32GiB).
And within each TensorCore, there lies our compute units and smaller memory buffers:
1. Matrix Multiply Unit (MXU)
- This is the key component of the TensorCore and is a 128x128 systolic array.
- We'll cover systolic arrays below.
2. Vector Unit (VPU)
- General elementwise operations (e.g. ReLU, pointwise add/mul, reductions)
3. Vector Memory (VMEM; 32MiB)
- Memory buffer. Data from HBM is copied into the VMEM before the TensorCore can do any computations.
4. Scalar Unit + Scalar Memory (SMEM; 10MiB)
- Tell the VPU and MXU what to do.
- Manages control flow, scalar operations, and memory address generation.
If you're coming from NVIDIA GPUs, there's some initial observations that might throw you off:
On-chip memory units (CMEM, VMEM, SMEM) on TPUs are much larger than L1, L2 caches on GPUs.
HBM on TPUs are also much smaller than HBM on GPUs.
There seems to be a lot less "cores" responsible for the computation.
This is the complete opposite of GPUs where they have smaller L1, L2 caches (256KB and 50MB, respectively for H100), larger HBM (80GB for H100), and tens of thousands of cores.
Before we go any further, recall that TPUs are capable of extremely high throughput just like GPUs. TPU v5p can achieve 500 TFLOPs/sec per chip and with a full pod of 8960 chips we can achieve approximately 4.45 ExaFLOPs/sec. The newest "Ironwood" TPUv7 is said to reach up to 42.5 ExaFLOPS/sec per pod (9216 chips).
To understand how TPUs achieve this, we need to understand their design philosophy.
TPU Design Philosophy
TPUs achieve amazing throughput and energy efficiency by relying on two large pillars and a key assumption: systolic arrays + pipelining, Ahead-of-Time (AoT) compilation, and the assumption that most operations can be expressed in a way that maps well to systolic arrays. Fortunately, in our modern DL era, matmuls comprise the bulk of computation, which are fit for systolic arrays.
TPU Design choice #1: Systolic Arrays + Pipelining
Q. What is a Systolic Array?
Systolic array is a hardware design architecture consisting of a grid of interconnected processing elements (PE). Each PE performs a small computation (e.g. multiply and accumulate) and passes the results to neighboring PEs.
The benefit of such a design is that once data is passed into a systolic array, additional control logic on how data should be processed is not required. Also, when given a large enough systolic array, there's no memory read/writes other than the input and output.
Due to their rigid organization, systolic arrays can only handle operations with fixed dataflow patterns, but fortunately matrix multiplication and convolutions fit perfectly in this regime.
Moreover, there's clear opportunities for pipelining to overlap computation with data movements. Here's a diagram below for a pipelined pointwise operation on a TPU.
Pipelined Pointwise Operation (from "How to Scale Your Model"
[4]
)
Aside: Downsides of Systolic Arrays - Sparsity
You can see how systolic arrays love dense matrices (i.e. When every PE is active nearly every cycle). However, the downside is that there's no performance improvements for sparse matrices of the same size: the same number of cycles will have to be performed where PEs are still doing work even for zero-valued eleme

data.article_summary: Claude Code宣布支持远程MCP服务器，用户可以将第三方工具和数据源集成到编码环境中，而无需管理本地服务器。通过连接MCP服务器，Claude Code能够访问如开发工具、项目管理系统和知识库等服务，并在其中执行操作。例如，与Sentry MCP服务器集成后，可以在终端中直接调试问题；与Linear MCP服务器集成后，可以获取项目和问题详情，减少切换界面的需要。远程MCP服务器由供应商维护，用户只需添加服务器URL，Claude Code支持原生OAuth以确保连接安全。该功能现已上线，用户可查看文档或MCP目录开始使用。

44312363.article_content:
Product
Remote MCP support in Claude Code
Jun 18, 2025
●
2 min
read
Today, we’re announcing support for remote MCP servers in Claude Code. Connect your favorite tools and data sources to personalize your coding experience without needing to manage local servers.
Using Claude Code as your primary development interface
Claude Code can access both tools and resources exposed by MCP servers, giving it the ability to pull context from your third-party services—such as dev tools, project management systems, and knowledge bases—and take actions within those services.
You can integrate Claude Code with any remote MCP server, and the growing ecosystem of servers means that new capabilities are constantly coming online.
For example, by integrating Claude Code with the Sentry MCP server, you can access errors and issues from Sentry. Then, you can debug using the context of those issues without leaving your terminal.
You can also integrate Claude Code with the Linear MCP server to work with the context of your active projects.
“Linear's MCP integration brings Linear projects and issues directly into Claude Code,” shares Tom Moor, Head of Engineering at Linear. “With structured, real-time context from Linear, Claude Code can pull in issue details and project status—engineers can now stay in flow when moving between planning, writing code, and managing issues. Fewer tabs, less copy-paste. Better software, faster.”
Seamless connections with minimal maintenance
Remote MCP servers offer a lower maintenance alternative to local servers: just add the vendor’s URL to Claude Code—no manual setup required. Vendors handle updates, scaling, and availability, so you can focus on building instead of managing server infrastructure.
Claude Code also features native OAuth support for remote MCP servers, ensuring secure connections to your existing accounts. Simply authenticate to your servers once, and Claude Code handles the rest—no API keys to manage or credentials to store.
Getting started
Remote MCP server support is available now in Claude Code. View the
documentation
to get started or explore our
MCP directory
with recommended servers.

data.title: Samsung embeds IronSource spyware app on phones across WANA
data.author: the-anarchist
data.article_summary: 这封公开信由SMEX组织撰写，呼吁三星公司对在西亚洲和北非（WANA）地区销售的A系列和M系列智能手机中预装的AppCloud软件保持透明度。AppCloud由以色列公司ironSource开发，深度集成于设备操作系统中，用户无法轻易移除或选择退出，且其隐私政策不透明，可能收集敏感个人数据。信中要求三星披露AppCloud的数据处理实践，提供简便的退出和移除选项，并重新考虑未来设备的预装策略，以尊重用户的隐私权。同时，SMEX请求与三星团队会面，进一步讨论这些问题。

44334167.article_content:
Back to News
Open Letter to Samsung: End Forced Israeli-Founded Bloatware Installations in the WANA Region
Appcloud
Invasive
ironSource
Written by
SMEX
Published on
05 May 2025
https://smex.org/open-letter-to-samsung-end-forced-israeli-app-installations-in-the-wana-region/
Copy link
In recent months, we have received numerous reports from users across West Asia and North Africa (WANA) expressing alarm over a little-known but deeply intrusive bloatware application—AppCloud—pre-installed on Samsung’s A and M series smartphones. Without users’ knowledge or consent, this bloatware collects sensitive personal data, cannot be removed without compromising device security, and offers no clear information about its privacy practices.
AppCloud, developed by the controversial Israeli-founded company ironSource (now owned by the American company
Unity
), is embedded into devices sold in countries where such affiliations carry legal implications. Despite the serious privacy and security risks, Samsung has offered no transparency on how AppCloud functions, what data it collects, or why users cannot opt out.
This open letter, addressed to Samsung, calls for immediate transparency, accountability, and dialogue. Users deserve to know what is installed on their devices and how their data is being used, especially amid Israel’s espionage campaigns in the region.
_________
To Whom it May Concern,
We are writing to urgently request that Samsung be transparent regarding the pre-installation of AppCloud on its A and M series smartphones, particularly in West Asia and North Africa (WANA). We ask that Samsung provide information about AppCloud’s privacy practices, opt-out and removal options, and that Samsung reconsider future pre-installations in light of privacy rights. We also request a meeting with Samsung teams to discuss these concerns further.
Since the expansion of Samsung’s
partnership
with ironSource in 2022, AppCloud has been embedded by default on
new A and M devices distributed in this region
.
According to our
analysis
, this intrusive software is
unremovable
, deeply integrated into the devices’ operating system, making it nearly impossible for regular users to uninstall it without root access, which voids warranties and poses security risks. Even disabling the bloatware is not effective as it can reappear after system updates.
The privacy policy is
opaque,
there is no accessible and transparent privacy policy for this bloatware and users are in the dark about what data is collected and how it is used. There is also no straightforward opt-out mechanism. The bloatware collects sensitive user data, including biometric information, IP addresses, device fingerprints.
The installation of AppCloud is done
without any consent
from the user, which violates GDPR provisions in the EU and relevant data protection laws in the WANA region states.
AppCloud is developed by ironSource,
an Israel-founded company (now acquired by American company Unity),
raising additional legal and ethical concerns in countries where Israeli companies are barred from operating, such as
Lebanon
. ironSource is notorious for its questionable practices regarding user consent and data privacy.
Samsung’s terms of service mention third party applications but do not specifically address AppCloud or ironSource, despite the significant data access and control granted to this bloatware app.
The forced installation of AppCloud
undermines the privacy and security rights of users in the MENA region and beyond.
The lack of transparency and control over personal data is particularly alarming given
Samsung’s
significant market share in the region
.
In light of these concerns, we respectfully request that Samsung:
Disclose the full privacy policy and data handling practices of AppCloud, making this information easily accessible to all users.
Offer a straightforward and effective method for users to opt out of AppCloud and remove it from their devices without compromising device functionality or warranty.
Provide a clear explanation for the decision to pre-install AppCloud on all A and M series devices in the WANA region.
Reconsider the continued pre-installation of AppCloud on future devices, in line with the right to privacy as established by Article 12 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
We also request a
meeting with the relevant Samsung teams
to discuss these issues in detail and to better understand the company’s approach to user privacy and data protection in the WANA region.
We look forward to your prompt response and to working together to ensure the privacy and security of all Samsung users.
Related
This article can be found in Arabic
here.
SMEX
About the author
SMEX is a registered Lebanese NGO that works to advance self-regulating information societies in the Middle East and North Africa.

data.title: Discover C++26's compile-time reflection
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: Herb Sutter宣布，C++26将引入编译时反射功能。反射允许程序访问代码结构，例如列举类的方法。C++的编译时反射是一项重要发展，将带来性能和简化代码的优势。以simdjson库为例，通过支持编译时反射，可以轻松将数据结构转换为JSON字符串，或从JSON文档转换回自定义类型。此外，还能简化SQL插入语句的生成，通过单个函数调用自动生成列名和值字符串。虽然代码看起来复杂，但能带来高度优化和安全的代码重用。未来几年，许多项目将因此得到简化。

44343084.article_content:
Herb Sutter just announced
that the verdict is in: C++26, the next version of C++, will include
compile-time
reflection.
Reflection in programming languages means that you have access the code’s own structure. For example, you can take a class, and enumerate its methods. For example, you could receive a class, check whether it contains a method that returns a string, call this method and get the string. Most programming languages have some form of reflection. For example, the good old Java does have complete reflection support.
However, C++ is getting compile-time reflection. It is an important development.
I announced a few months ago that thanks to joint work with Francisco Geiman Thiesen,
the performance-oriented JSON library simdjson would support compile-time reflection
as soon as mainstream compilers support it.
This allows you to take your own data structure and convert it to a JSON string without any effort, and at high speed:
kid k{12, "John", {"car", "ball"}};
simdjson::to_json(k);
// would generate {"age": 12, "name": "John", "toys": ["car", "ball"]}
And you can also go back, given a JSON document, you can get back an instance of your custom type:
kid k = doc.get<kid>();

主要讨论点：Firefox浏览器的多行标签页功能、树状标签页自动化管理、是否应为浏览器付费

不同观点：
• [replete] 支持使用Firefox的多行标签页CSS hack，认为在研究期间使用5到6行的标签页是常见的，有助于按时间顺序管理标签页。不过该方案有副作用，即标签页重新排序会半失效，需要通过CMD/CTRL+点击来解决"trails"问题。

• [pona-a] 支持类似的工作流，使用Sideberry插件进行标签页管理，但指出仍需手动组织。进一步提出树状标签浏览器需要某种脚本自动化，例如自动关闭重复标签、根据交互行为对标签进行分类和管理，以减少手动组织标签页的时间。

• [unixhero] 对浏览器的外观设计表示欣赏，但因为不愿意订阅软件，所以不会考虑使用付费浏览器。

• [JumpCrisscross] 表示愿意为类似的扩展付费，但不愿意为整个浏览器付费。

• [elasticventures] 赞赏"Trails"概念，但认为其 monetization（货币化）策略有问题。

• [SeriousM] 认为为浏览器付费就像为呼吸空气付费一样不合理，尤其是考虑到用户通常会使用大量其他扩展，并且浏览器的网站兼容性问题未被充分讨论。

• [mgd] 提到Nyxt Browser已经具备相关功能，暗示不需要为类似功能付费或使用特定浏览器。

• [BaudouinVH] 强烈反对为浏览器付费，即使自己有ADHD（注意力缺陷多动障碍），仍认为这不合理。

• [metalman] 使用书签作为项目管理工具，并通过特定浏览器（stoutner）的设置功能对书签进行进一步管理，例如控制音视频自动播放。同时指出，只有当软件有实际回报、可转售且有自动升级时，才会考虑付费。

补充讨论：
- 关于是否应为浏览器或其功能付费存在明显争议，焦点在于用户认为浏览器作为基础工具不应单独收费，且扩展和兼容性问题未得到充分解决。
- 树状标签页自动化管理被认为是提高标签页管理效率的一个潜在解决方案，但目前仍需手动操作。
- 不同的用户偏好和浏览器功能（如Firefox的CSS hack、Nyxt Browser的内置功能）使得讨论中出现了多种解决方案的比较。

data.title: A brief history of hardware epidemics
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了计算机硬件中的三次大规模故障事件。首先是1999-2007年的"电容瘟疫"，由于制造商使用劣质电容器，导致电脑主板等部件过热、漏液甚至起火，影响包括iMac G5和eMacs在内的设备。其次是2006-2017年无铅焊料带来的问题，特别是在高性能显卡中，因无铅焊料不如含铅焊料可靠，导致包括MacBook Pro和iMac在内的设备故障率增加。最后是2015-2019年苹果推出的蝶式键盘，因设计缺陷，导致按键卡住、重复或完全失灵。这些事件均对产品寿命和用户体验造成了负面影响。
